title: Poulet Rôti
subtitle: French roast chicken with butter and thyme
excerpt: A whole chicken roasted the French way: buttered all over, seasoned generously, and roasted at high heat until the skin is lacquered and crisp. Simple and perfect.

recipe.sourceNotes: Poulet rôti is the cornerstone of French home cooking, and roast chicken is often cited as a litmus test of a cook's competence. The French method emphasises high heat, generous seasoning, and frequent basting to achieve very crisp skin and juicy meat. In Paris, the scent of rôtisseries turning chickens over open flames is famous. Julia Child gave the definitive English-language instructions in Mastering the Art of French Cooking (1961), emphasising the importance of a very hot oven and a bird that has been brought to room temperature before roasting.

recipeTools.notes: A close-fitting tin so the juices don't burn.
Check the thickest part of the thigh: 75 C is done.

content.text: Take the chicken out of the fridge an hour before cooking. A cold bird going into a hot oven is the most common cause of unevenly cooked meat: the outside overcooks before the inside is done. Season the inside of the cavity as well as the outside. Baste with the pan juices every 20 minutes. Rest the bird for at least 10 minutes before carving: the juices need to redistribute.
Take the chicken out of the fridge 1 hour before cooking. Heat the oven to 220 C / fan 200 C / gas 7.

Rub the softened butter all over the outside of the chicken and under the skin of the breast. Season generously with salt and pepper inside and out. Put the lemon halves, garlic, and half the thyme sprigs inside the cavity. Lay the remaining thyme under the bird.

Place the chicken breast-side up in a roasting tin. Roast for 15 minutes at 220 C, then reduce to 190 C / fan 170 C / gas 5 and roast for a further 55 to 60 minutes, basting every 20 minutes with the pan juices. The chicken is done when the juices run clear when you pierce the thigh, or a thermometer reads 75 C at the thickest point of the thigh.
Rest the chicken uncovered for at least 10 minutes before carving. Serve with the pan juices spooned over.
